decision: Keep R4 two-pointer reader and separately prepared predicate. Caching stride==1 in predicate padding loses on complete preparation/one-shot commands; fewer selected hot-path instructions do not establish a performance improvement.
limits: Five counterbalanced trials of warm complete commands, not cold memory, owner publication or a complete Frame consumer.
Duplicate is byte-identical before ELF, measured with common argv0/cwd/user args; it is a negative control, never a correction factor.

Maintained shared decode/compare routes bypass the prepared predicate; their x86 timing changes do not establish direct flag/preparation work in those bodies. Linked layout remains part of these actual executables.
The ARM overlap-copy/store-forwarding hazard is emitted-code evidence; its causal contribution to the measured one-shot loss is not established by this comparison.
Only the candidate header differs from frozen R4. Later core writer API corrections and live Frame algorithms retain their separate qualification.
reproduction: Run handle-boundaries/predicate-results.py on the two recovered results directories. Select metrics wall_ns_per_window and cpu_ns_per_query without merging their units or correcting by duplicate.
selection: All filters wall ns/window and all blocks CPU ns/query: 360+108 per profile. Block CPU ns/traversal and ns/block are derivable from retained structural counters and were validated by the full reader; their redundant rows remain in ignored output and original worker records.
status: rejected; candidate header was never applied to live Ikea
